propositions: The reconciler's committed .bridge_state cache accounts for 92% (approx 950 MiB) of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch, with negligible content changes but excessive churn in bookkeeping fields baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass that defeat git delta compression.

Deleting the timestamp field baseline_advanced_at and moving last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping to a separate .bridge_state/get_rotation.json file reduces marginal cost per bindings.json version from 12.79 KB to approximately 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement).

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/filter/fast-import pipeline can reduce the existing tickets branch from 1.1+ GiB to ~98 MiB (8.4%) while preserving all commits and merges, with byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add of current .bridge_state files.

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners requiring durable state in git; moving .bridge_state off-branch is rejected because the convergence loop self-heals binding drift and the content/churn levers suffice.

Mixed-version compatibility during rollout requires A2-1 to retain legacy field writes, A2-2 to stop legacy writes but read max(sidecar, legacy), and rollback to require an explicit quiesced window with bundle restoration and writer re-cloning on epoch mismatch.

Rollout gates for A2-2 and reclaim (A6-1) replace fixed-delay windows with direct behavioral evidence: descendant workflow execution, explicit host refresh, live writer epoch-refusal probes, and operator attestation of zero sessions and stopped processes before publication.
